settings.showTreemap.tip: Shows or hides the treemap below the tree and table. When hidden, tree and table use the full height.
rule.temp-user.title: Temporary files (user)
rule.temp-user.text: Scratch space for programs and installers. Anything newer than two days is kept - it might still be in use.
rule.temp-windows.title: Temporary files (Windows)
rule.temp-windows.text: Temp folder of Windows itself and its services. Needs administrator rights; anything newer than two days is kept.
rule.windows-update.title: Windows Update downloads
rule.windows-update.text: Update packages that were already downloaded. Not needed after installation; Windows downloads them again if required. The last ten days are kept in case an update is still waiting for a restart.
rule.delivery-optimization.title: Delivery Optimization
rule.delivery-optimization.text: Update pieces Windows shares with other PCs. Pure cache.
rule.error-reports.title: Error reports and crash dumps
rule.error-reports.text: Memory dumps and crash reports. Only useful for troubleshooting, otherwise worthless.
rule.memory-dump.title: Memory dump of the last blue screen
rule.memory-dump.text: MEMORY.DMP - the complete RAM at the last system crash. Only useful for troubleshooting.
rule.recycle-bin.title: Recycle Bin
rule.recycle-bin.text: Deleted files take up space until the Recycle Bin is emptied. It gets emptied, not moved.
rule.browser-chrome.title: Google Chrome - cache
rule.browser-chrome.text: Cached web pages, scripts and graphics. Bookmarks, passwords and sign-ins stay. Close Chrome first, otherwise locked files are left behind.
rule.browser-edge.title: Microsoft Edge - cache
rule.browser-edge.text: Cached web pages, scripts and graphics. Favorites, passwords and sign-ins stay. Close Edge first.
rule.browser-brave.title: Brave - cache
rule.browser-brave.text: Cached web pages, scripts and graphics. Bookmarks, passwords and sign-ins stay. Close Brave first.
rule.browser-firefox.title: Firefox - cache
rule.browser-firefox.text: Cached web pages. Bookmarks, passwords and sign-ins are stored elsewhere and stay. Close Firefox first.
rule.shader-cache.title: Graphics card shader caches
rule.shader-cache.text: Precompiled graphics programs from DirectX, NVIDIA and AMD. They rebuild themselves - games load a little longer or stutter briefly on the first start afterwards.
rule.steam-shadercache.title: Steam - shader cache
rule.steam-shadercache.text: Precompiled shaders per game. Steam downloads or rebuilds them when needed.
rule.steam-temp.title: Steam - temporary files
rule.steam-downloading.title: Steam - unfinished downloads
rule.steam-downloading.text: Leftovers of cancelled or paused downloads. Only clean up when nothing is downloading in Steam - otherwise the download starts over.
rule.driver-downloads.title: Old driver installation files
rule.driver-downloads.text: Extracted driver packages from NVIDIA and AMD. The installed driver no longer needs them.
rule.app-discord.title: Discord - cache
rule.app-discord.text: Cached images, videos and scripts. Messages are stored on the server. Quit Discord first.
rule.app-spotify.title: Spotify - cache
rule.app-spotify.text: Cached tracks for faster playback. Downloaded offline tracks are stored elsewhere.
rule.app-electron.title: Other program caches
rule.app-electron.text: Web caches of other programs (Teams, Slack, VS Code and many more that use a browser internally). They rebuild themselves; quit the programs first.
rule.dev-package-caches.title: Package caches (npm, pip, Yarn, Gradle)
rule.dev-package-caches.text: Packages downloaded in advance. They are downloaded again on the next install - costs time and bandwidth once.
rule.dev-nuget.title: NuGet packages (.NET)
rule.dev-nuget.text: Every .NET package ever used. The next build downloads what it needs again.
rule.dev-node-modules.title: node_modules of dormant projects
rule.dev-node-modules.text: Dependencies of JavaScript projects that have not changed in three months. "npm install" restores them when needed.
rule.old-installers.title: Old installers in the Downloads folder
rule.old-installers.text: Setup files and disk images that have been sitting there for more than six months. The program was installed long ago - or never will be.
rule.hint-hiberfil.title: Hibernation file (hiberfil.sys)
rule.hint-hiberfil.text: Holds the RAM contents for hibernation and fast startup. If you use neither, you can turn it off.
rule.hint-hiberfil.advice: Command prompt as administrator: powercfg /h off - turns off hibernation and fast startup, and the file disappears.
rule.hint-windows-old.title: Previous Windows installation
rule.hint-windows-old.text: Kept after a major Windows update so you can go back to the old version. Windows removes it by itself after about ten days.
rule.hint-windows-old.advice: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > "Previous Windows installation(s)". After that there is no going back.
rule.hint-winsxs.title: Component store (WinSxS)
rule.hint-winsxs.text: Old versions of system files after updates. The size shown is misleading: much of it is hard links to files in System32. Never delete it by hand.
rule.hint-restore-points.title: Restore points
rule.hint-restore-points.text: Shadow copies for System Restore, in System Volume Information.
rule.hint-restore-points.advice: Control Panel > System > System Protection > Configure: limit disk space or delete old points.

xlsx.relocate.text: Folders using 500 MB or more, movable by their nature and not blocked by the app's safety rules - the same selection as in the Relocate tab. Online-only files from iCloud and OneDrive do not count; they take no local space. A shortlist to look at - nothing here is touched automatically.

ai.denied: {0:N0} folders were not readable and are missing from the totals
ai.estimate: "On disk" is rounded to the cluster size, not read from the file system
ai.reliability: How reliable are the age figures
ai.accessUsable: Access times are **usable**. "Unused for" refers to the last activity, i.e. the later of modification and access.
ai.accessNotUsable: Access times are **not usable**. "Unused for" is therefore based on the modification date alone.
ai.folderAge: For folders, the most recent activity in the whole subtree counts: a folder is only considered cold if not a single file in it was touched recently.

ai.findingsNote: Pattern matching, not a recommendation. Rating: *safe* = rebuilds itself or is junk, *careful* = look first, *risky* = only with good reason.
ai.findingsHeader: | Rule | Rating | Size | Unused | Path | Note |
ai.taskText: This report is the basis for a cleanup and relocation decision. Wanted: what can go, what can move to another drive, what must stay. Folders that move stay visible at the old path as a junction; programs do not notice. Answer as a list with path, action (delete / relocate / keep) and a short reason.

overview.largest.title: Largest files
overview.largest.text: By space used on disk - online-only files do not count. Click shows the folder in the tree.
cleanup.recycleAll: safe items to Recycle Bin too
cleanup.recycleAll.tip: Default: caches and temp files are deleted permanently - in the Recycle Bin they would keep taking up space. Everything marked careful always goes to the Recycle Bin.
cleanup.systemFolder: Located in a system folder - without administrator rights much of it stays.
cleanup.doubleClick: Double-click opens the location in Explorer.
cleanup.intro.title: Look first, then clean up
cleanup.intro.text: SizeShift looks for caches, temp files, old installers and other space hogs. Choose the drives to search - nothing is deleted until you confirm.
relocate.suggestions.tip: Large folders from the last scan that can be moved by their nature.
relocate.refresh.tip: Reload both sides: folders, links, free space and sizes.
relocate.go.tip: Check the checked folders and relocate them into the folder selected on the right. A summary to confirm comes first.
relocate.back.tip: Move checked relocated folders (link icon) back to their original location.
relocate.newFolder.tip: Create a new folder in the selected folder, e.g. D:\Games.
relocate.toBin.tip: A second safety net next to the verified copy. But the space on C: is only freed once the Recycle Bin is emptied.
relocate.delete.tip: Space freed immediately. The verified copy on the target drive is then the only copy.
relocate.fullHash.tip: The default is a sample (all small files, the largest ones and a random share). A full check takes much longer for large games.
relocate.linkNote: A link stays at the old location – programs and games find everything as usual.
docs.open.tip: Open Documents\SizeShift: history, log, exports and AI reports.

start.text: Tap a drive - SizeShift scans in seconds and shows what is large, what nobody has touched in years and what can move to another drive.

startup.lockedHint: Entries with a lock apply to all users. They can only be switched while SizeShift runs as administrator (button at the top right).
rule.privacy-history.title: {0}: history and last session
rule.privacy-history.text: Visited pages, address bar suggestions and the most recently open tabs of {0}. Passwords, bookmarks, extensions and settings are left alone. Deleted permanently - in the recycle bin the data would still be there. Close {0} first, otherwise it is skipped.
rule.privacy-cookies.title: {0}: cookies
rule.privacy-cookies.text: The cookies of {0}. Afterwards you are signed out of every website and have to sign in again; passwords, bookmarks and settings stay. Deleted permanently. Close {0} first, otherwise it is skipped.
rule.privacy-forms-firefox.title: Firefox: form data and last session
rule.privacy-forms-firefox.text: Saved form entries and the most recently open tabs of Firefox. SizeShift leaves the Firefox history itself in place: it lives in the same file as the bookmarks, and those should not disappear with it - use Ctrl+Shift+Del in Firefox for that. Close Firefox first, otherwise it is skipped.
rule.privacy-recent.title: Recently used files
rule.privacy-recent.text: The Windows "Recent" list in Explorer and the jump lists in the Start menu and taskbar. The files themselves of course stay, only the list is emptied.
rule.privacy-thumbnails.title: Thumbnail cache
rule.privacy-thumbnails.text: Preview images Explorer has stored for pictures and videos - including files deleted long ago. They are rebuilt the next time a folder is opened. Whatever Explorer currently holds open stays.
rule.privacy-clipboard.title: Clipboard
rule.privacy-clipboard.text: The current clipboard content, for example a copied password or text.
rule.privacy-clipboard.advice: To clear the clipboard history (Windows+V), go to Settings > System > Clipboard > "Clear clipboard data".
rule.privacy-dns.title: DNS cache
rule.privacy-dns.text: Windows remembers which internet addresses were resolved recently - which reveals the sites that were visited. Clearing it is harmless; the list fills up again while browsing. Same as "ipconfig /flushdns".

Please derive from it: where can space be gained, what can move to another disk, which startup entries can be turned off without problems, and is anything notable about the hardware or drives? Everything was only read, nothing was changed.

procs.report.tip: Save the recording as a Markdown file – for an AI to evaluate.
procs.intro.title: What is running on this PC – and what is eating it?
procs.intro.text: Pick a duration and press “Record” – keep using the PC as usual. Every few seconds SizeShift measures the processor, memory and disk use of every program, then shows who used how much and who started it. The measurement itself costs less than one percent of performance. As administrator, protected system processes are included too.
procreport.title: Process report: {0}
procreport.created: Recorded from {0} for {1} ({2} samples) with SizeShift.
procreport.forAi: Recording of every running program on this PC, created by SizeShift – for an AI to evaluate. Please derive from it: which programs use notably much processor, memory or disk, which of them are unknown or unnecessary, which program belongs to which (column “Started by”), and what can be closed or removed from startup? Everything was only measured, nothing was changed.
procreport.notElevated: Recorded without administrator rights: path and measurements are missing for some protected system processes.
procreport.units: CPU as a percentage of total computing power (all cores together = 100 %). Memory as working set, all instances of a program combined. Disk = read / written during the recording.
procreport.footer: Created with SizeShift. Only measured, nothing changed.
procs.showAll.tip: Also show programs that used hardly any processor, memory or disk.
procs.adminHint: Without administrator rights, many Windows services (svchost) report no values – restart “As administrator” at the top for complete figures.
procreport.services: “svchost.exe (…)” is a Windows service host; the names in brackets are the services running inside.
